final_strategies.rationale: Four blocks: (1) exposure agent, made of core pesticide classes, aerial/drift terms, named actives and a narrow drinking-water-contaminant phrase set; (2) birth and infant outcomes; (3) a context block for environmental, agricultural, geographic or policy settings, which acts as a precision device against biomonitoring-only, occupational-only and toxicology records; (4) NOT blocks for animal/in-vitro studies and malaria bed nets. Recall: 9/9 seeds, 15/17 validation set 1 (both misses have outcomes outside SQ1), 20/20 validation set 2. Trade-off: the context block cuts 3233 records to 1859 (-42.5%) with zero loss on 46 known in-scope items.

volume_estimate_after_dedup: About 1,850 to 2,100 unique records for title/abstract screening. This is an estimate: no deduplication was run. Basis: OpenAlex final string 1,821 after type exclusions (1,859 before); PubMed adapted string 787, expected to overlap OpenAlex heavily, adding perhaps 50-150 records through MeSH; ranked supplements (top 100 of the PubMed-index framings, Scholar Gateway) mostly duplicates; grey literature about 10-30 items. OpenAlex also holds internal duplicates (preprint plus published versions, Faculty Opinions records, conference abstracts; 115 conference abstracts in the set), so expect some shrinkage. The sensitive variant would raise the OpenAlex input to about 3,230.
issues_and_limits: Transport: firecrawl_scrape to OpenAlex hit the Firecrawl rate limit (shared quota, 11-13 requests/min). WebFetch could not resolve api.openalex.org. All later OpenAlex and E-utilities calls went through mcp__Parallel_Search__web_fetch to the same public APIs. One OpenAlex call returned HTTP 429 and its replacement was re-run successfully.
Counts are a snapshot from 2026-10-11 and the OpenAlex index changes over time. The protocol should record the run date and the exact URL.

OpenAlex has no wildcard or no-stem option in this API version (both return HTTP 400). Morphology relies on its stemmer, so British spellings (foetal) and spelling variants were added by hand. Truncation-dependent variants such as 'agrotoxic*' may be incomplete.

The NOT blocks apply to the whole title and abstract. Dropping 'mice', 'rats' etc. removed 242 records from the context-filtered set, and the top-cited of them were animal or in-vitro studies. A human study whose abstract mentions a rodent finding could still be lost. The bed-net NOT uses net-specific phrases so that 'insecticide-treated seeds' studies are kept.

The context block is a precision device. It lost none of the 46 known items, but ecological studies with unusual wording could fall outside it. The sensitive variant (3,233) is documented as a fallback.

The outcome block deliberately excludes neurodevelopment, childhood cancer and adult outcomes. That is why it misses Lai 2017 and Fletcher & Noghanibehambari 2023, which are probably ineligible anyway but relevant for design. Brainerd & Menon 2014 (fertilizer agrichemicals) is retrieved only through the child-mortality terms, and its eligibility is borderline: fertilizer is not a pesticide.

The two validation sets were drawn from the PubMed-index semantic searches and web searches, independently of the Boolean design, but they are small (37 items) and skewed toward epidemiology. The economics coverage rests mainly on the 9 seeds.

Elsevier abstracts show as null through the API yet are searchable (Camacho & Mejia was matched on abstract words). Screening exports from OpenAlex will lack abstracts for these records, so plan to fetch them from Crossref or PubMed.

The Firecrawl research index and PubMed do not cover JAERE or ReStud, and Scholar Gateway covers Wiley only. For SQ1 the economics literature therefore depends on OpenAlex plus grey literature plus citation chasing.
The Maertens (2017) atrazine, Renewable Fuel Standard and fetal malformation working paper, cited in IZA DP 12164, could not be located; follow it up through the IZA DP reference list.

This was English-only calibration. Portuguese and Spanish terms (agrotóxico, pulverização aérea, peso ao nascer, malformação congênita) and LILACS/SciELO are left to the other-language agent; 'agrotoxic' and 'plaguicide' were included as English loanwords.
syntax_findings: OpenAlex title_and_abstract.search honours uppercase AND, OR and NOT, parentheses and quoted phrases. Set algebra checks out exactly: pesticide = 316,429; "birth weight" = 174,496; AND = 458; OR = 490,467 = A + B - A∧B; A NOT B = 315,971 = A - A∧B. The OQL echo in meta.x_query confirms how each query was parsed.
Lowercase 'and' is not an operator: it is parsed as a search term and, as a stopword, leaves the count unchanged. Space-separated terms are implicitly ANDed.

Stemming is always on: 'pesticide' and 'pesticides' give the same count, and quoted phrases are matched as 'stemmed' phrases. A '*' wildcard returns HTTP 400. The title_and_abstract.search.no_stem filter returns HTTP 400 in the current API.
Multiple filters are ANDed with commas, and negation works on facets (type:!paratext etc.). group_by cannot be combined with select (HTTP 400) but works without it.
Known-item recall works by prefixing doi:<DOI1>|<DOI2>|... to the search filter. Up to 26 DOIs in one pipe list worked, and URLs of about 4,200 characters were accepted.
Elsevier records return abstract_inverted_index = null yet are still matched on abstract words by title_and_abstract.search.

PubMed E-utilities ([tiab], truncation *, [mh], [doi]) is reachable through Parallel web_fetch. Unknown DOIs come back in warninglist.quotedphrasesnotfound, which shows directly which seeds are not indexed.
